messages.author: 4ddc99c6029ba75d
messages.subject: question about the borders function
parts:
Hi all:
Does anyone know how to use the borders function with a shapefile
imported into R
using the readOGR function? I don't get an error message but instead
it creates a bigger
plot area below the shapefile. Please consider the example below after
downloading the
shapefile from this link:

https://secure.filesanywhere.com/fs/v.aspx?v=897263875a6472a99baa

library(rgdal)
library(maptools)
library(ggplot2)
libray(maps)
dsn="C:/PathToShapefile"
wolves.map <- readOGR(dsn=dsn, layer="PNW_wolf_habitat_grid")
wolves.mapDF <- as.data.frame(wolves.map)
gpclibPermit()
wolves.ds <- fortify(wolves.map,region="GRID2_ID")

# Rename the 'GRID2'_ID to 'id' to to be able to merge with the
shapefile wolves.map
wolves.mapDF <- rename(wolves.mapDF,c(GRID2_ID="id"))
names(wolves.mapDF)

# merge the shapefile wolves.ds and wolves.mapDF dataframe to be able
to use the wolves.mapDF variables with ggplot2
wolves.ggmap <- merge(wolves.ds, wolves.mapDF, by = "id", all = TRUE)
wolves.ggmap <- wolves.ggmap[order(wolves.ggmap$order), ]
head(wolves.ggmap)

# Shapefile of 5 states, plot using ggplot2
wolves.plot <- ggplot(wolves.ds,aes(long,lat,group=group)) +
geom_polygon(colour='white',fill='lightblue')
wolves.plot
wolves.plot + borders("state") # doesn't work when borders function is
added to the plot

I was trying to generate a map with the 5 states and place it on top
of the above shapefile but the
column names are different,,perhaps will try to merge both datasets?

# How to show the state borders of Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Montana
and Wyoming on map?
#library(maps)
# extract county outlines and names from maps() database
#areaStudy <- map_data("state", c("oregon","washington",
"montana","wyoming", "idaho"))
#head(areaStudy)

messages.author: 45a85351148578ad
messages.subject: RE: question about the borders function
parts:
Hi Felipe,

In my opinión, the problem is that borders import the data directly with
geographical coordinates. Consider the following alternative (sessionInfo()
as ps);

##########
proj4string(wolves.map)

areaStudy <- map_data("state", c("oregon","washington","montana","wyoming",
"idaho"))

head(areaStudy)
areaStudy[, 1:2] <- project(as.matrix(areaStudy[, 1:2]),
proj4string(wolves.map)) # from rgdal, project the coordinates of state
polygons
areaStudy <- areaStudy[order(areaStudy$order), ]
wolves.plot <- ggplot(wolves.ds,aes(long,lat,group=group)) +
geom_polygon(colour='white',fill='lightblue') +
geom_path(data = areaStudy, aes(group = group)) # add just the
border to experiment
wolves.plot
###########

You can also so the converse (project the coordinates in wolves.map to
geographic). Think this will allow to use coord_map ...
Hope this helps,
fernando

messages.subject: RE: question about the borders function
parts:
Hi Felipe,

You can use rgdal::project for this (e.g. see the argument inv in ?project).
I put some code bellow based on your example. For a general overview of R
spatial capabilities, check http://cran.r-project.org/web/views/Spatial.html


I guess nevertheless that the projection used in your shapefile (Albers) is
probably appropriate (e.g. I think it is widely used in USA and Canada?).

Hope this helps,
fernando


library(rgdal)
library(maptools)
library(ggplot2)
library(maps)

dsn="C:/PathToShapefile"
# original at
https://secure.filesanywhere.com/fs/v.aspx?v=897263875a6472a99baa

wolves.map <- readOGR(dsn=dsn, layer="PNW_wolf_habitat_grid")
wolves.mapDF <- as.data.frame(wolves.map)
gpclibPermit()
wolves.ds <- fortify(wolves.map,region="GRID2_ID")

# Rename the 'GRID2'_ID to 'id' to to be able to merge with the shapefile
wolves.map
wolves.mapDF <- rename(wolves.mapDF,c(GRID2_ID="id"))
names(wolves.mapDF)
# merge the shapefile wolves.ds and wolves.mapDF dataframe to be able
# to use the wolves.mapDF variables with ggplot2

wolves.ggmap <- merge(wolves.ds, wolves.mapDF, by = "id", all = TRUE)
wolves.ggmap <- wolves.ggmap[order(wolves.ggmap$order), ]
head(wolves.ggmap)

areaStudy <- map_data("state", c("oregon","washington","montana","wyoming",
"idaho"))
head(areaStudy)

wolves.plot <- ggplot(wolves.ggmap, aes(long, lat, group = group)) +
geom_polygon(colour = I('white'), fill = I('lightblue')) +
geom_path(data = areaStudy, aes(group = group)) + # add just the
border to experiment
coord_map(project = "albers", lat0 = 23, lat1 = 29.5)
wolves.plot

############################################################################
##
